land.text: Judah round Jerusalem, a Neo-Babylonian province before the Persian conquest of Babylon in 539

predecessors.note: The kingdom-of-judah dossier ends in -586; the pages opened here do not describe 586-539.

land.text: Yehud, 'incorporated into the Hellenistic empires' after c. 332 BCE

successors.note: The page's infobox ends the province 'c. 332 BCE' and names no conqueror.

capitals.name: Mizpah
capitals.note: 'Mizpah continued as the provincial capital for over a century.' The coordinate (Tell en-Nasbeh) is the usual identification and is not on the page.

capitals.name: Jerusalem
capitals.note: 'From 445 BCE onwards, it was once more the main city of Yehud.'

correction.text: the province, 'from around Bethel in the north to near Hebron in the south'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row; the Achaemenid Empire shape holds this land). The page gives no area ('The entire population of the province remained around 30,000'; Jerusalem 2 to 2.5 hectares in the Persian period). A 32 km circle round Jerusalem with a 10 km circle at Hebron (about 3,800 km2) is a reading of Bethel-to-Hebron; the east-west extent is not on the page.

region.text: the province of Yehud, from Bethel to near Hebron

ledger.note: 539 BCE: the Persians organise Yehud as a province. 'Upon the Persian conquest of Babylon in 539 BCE, the Achaemenid Empire established its own Yehud province'; infobox 'c. 539 BCE-c. 332 BCE'. In 538 Cyrus 'decreed that the deportees in Babylon could return to Yehud' and appointed Sheshbazzar governor; no land changed (a 538 'gain from nobody' marker was removed by reviewer me-05-x, 2026-10-19).

539 BCE: Yehud is one of 'twenty provinces or administrative subunits in the large satrapy of Eber-nari'; the Achaemenid governors (Sheshbazzar appointed 538) rule it, so it is drawn as the Achaemenid Empire's tinted dependency, not as sovereign land.
445 BCE: Jerusalem again becomes the main city of Yehud, replacing Mizpah (provincial capital 'for over a century'); Nehemiah is dated to the second half of the fifth century.

332 BCE: the Persian province ends. The infobox gives 'c. 332 BCE'; the page says it 'lasted for just over two centuries before being incorporated into the Hellenistic empires' and does not name Alexander.
332 BCE: Yehud passes to the Macedonian conquerors (the page: 'incorporated into the Hellenistic empires'; the conqueror is the macedonian-empire dossier's reading).

certainty.note: Only the north-south span (Bethel to near Hebron) is on the page; the borders with Samaria, Idumea and the coast are not.

sources.title: Yehud Medinata
sources.note: Province 539-332, satrapy Eber-nari, governors, Mizpah then Jerusalem, Bethel to Hebron, population 30,000.

notes: One page (budget 1-2). Yehud is a province, not a sovereign state: type colony, a dependency drawn as a vassal tint of the Achaemenid Empire, whose Cliopatria shape already contains the land; the researcher accepts that the renderer may prefer to leave Yehud as detail inside achaemenid-empire. The 538 return of the deportees is in the found event's note (reviewer me-05-x removed the 538 'gain from nobody' marker: a gain must move land). The kingdom-of-judah dossier (me-04-b) ends in -586 and judea (me-05-f) starts in -142: the pages opened do not cover the Neo-Babylonian province of 586-539 nor the Ptolemaic and Seleucid Judea of 332-142, both unmapped gaps. The Ptolemaic and Seleucid periods are in those two dossiers' ledgers only as events of Coele-Syria. Mizpah's coordinate is the usual site, not from the page.
